terminal.capture: direct PTY with normalized stable markers

normalization: Binary paths, synthetic HOME/HERMES_HOME paths, PTY paths, timestamps, raw redraw bytes, and setup-state contents are omitted or represented by stable structural markers.

The replay enters only Full setup, skips the unconfigured provider, and either cancels the displayed local backend or accepts it before cancelling at the platform picker; no provider value, model value, credentials, OAuth action, endpoint secret, or platform selection is entered.

The existing config assertion remains limited to the Hades non-secret baseline. The new sidecar is an explicit Hades-owned extension and is represented only by its known structural markers, byte stability, and temporary-file absence; it is not claimed as Hermes YAML parity.
The two fresh cases separate backend cancellation from accepted-backend platform cancellation so a later boundary cannot hide an earlier mutation.
unknowns: Hermes exact scalar values, YAML ordering, backup contents, platform-specific setup, provider discovery, credentials, OAuth, network behavior, and successful later setup remain unknown.
Hades does not read this sidecar to establish provider readiness; config alone and the sidecar alone must not imply a ready provider session.
The sidecar records only the observed bounded local backend and empty platform boundary; selected platforms and all later platform persistence remain unknown.
